reason: E1 supports the use of laser-clad TiAl-based coatings with Cu to improve hardness and wear resistance on TC4, and E2 supports that UB treatment increases coating hardness by ~20%, but neither provides direct evidence for the specific (TiAl)93Cu5Ni2 composition, the combined sequential process, or the claimed submicron grain refinement and compressive stress mechanisms.
premises: Laser cladding of TiAl-based coatings on TC4 (Ti-6Al-4V) can increase hardness and reduce wear rate.
Addition of Cu in TiAl-based laser cladding coatings enhances hardness and wear resistance.
Ultrasonic burnishing (UB) treatment of metallic coatings increases surface hardness by about 20%.
UB treatment induces grain refinement and compressive residual stresses in metallic coatings.
